claim: Mice lacking Pum2 show apparent 'motorization' of layers IV and V of primary somatosensory cortex (S1), characterized by dramatic expansion of cells co-expressing Sox5 and Bcl11b/Ctip2.

evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bcl11b and Rorb mRNAs were observed as discrete foci primarily in the cytoplasm of post-mitotic neurons in layer IV/V of the developing pS.
source: Bcl11b and Rorb mRNAs were observed as discrete foci primarily in the cytoplasm, whereas Sox5 mRNA foci were detected in both the nucleus and cytoplasm (Figure 10a and b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10a and b.

claim: Sox5 mRNA foci were detected in both the nucleus and cytoplasm of post-mitotic neurons in layer IV/V of the developing pS.
source: Bcl11b and Rorb mRNAs were observed as discrete foci primarily in the cytoplasm, whereas Sox5 mRNA foci were detected in both the nucleus and cytoplasm (Figure 10a and b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10a and b.

claim: Cytoplasmic mRNA foci overlapped with the diffuse staining seen throughout the cytoplasm for both Pum2 and TDP-43.
source: Cytoplasmic mRNA foci overlapped with the diffuse staining seen throughout the cytoplasm for both Pum2 and TDP-43 (Figure 10a and b).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10a and b.

claim: Both Sox5, Bcl11b, and Rorb mRNAs and the RBPs Pum2 and TDP-43 that regulate them are present in the cytoplasm of post-mitotic neurons in developing pS.
source: These data demonstrate that both these mRNAs and the RBPs that regulate them are present in the cytoplasm of post-mitotic neurons in developing pS, suggesting that they could potentially interact there in neuronal messenger ribonucleoprotein (mRNP) complexes.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10a and b.

claim: Sox5, Bcl11b, and Rorb mRNAs and the RBPs Pum2 and TDP-43 could potentially interact in neuronal messenger ribonucleoprotein (mRNP) complexes in the cytoplasm of post-mitotic neurons in developing pS.

claim: Increased levels of both hTDP-43 and hTDP-43A315T proteins were detected in the cytoplasm at P0.

evidence: The claim is based on inference from the observation of increased cytoplasmic hTDP-43 levels.

claim: No significant interaction of Fezf2 mRNA with Pum2 or Cux1 mRNA with either Pum2 or TDP-43 was detected relative to 18S rRNA in UV-CLIPs.
source: We did not see significant interaction of Fezf2 mRNA with Pum2 or Cux1 mRNA with either protein relative to 18S rRNA, consistent with our finding that neither these mRNAs nor the encoded proteins showed altered regulation in developing neocortex in the Pum2 cKO or TDP43A315T lines.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 10c.

claim: Both Pum2 and TDP-43 can directly interact with specific mRNAs encoding layer IV/V neuronal identity determinants in vivo in the cytoplasm of cells in the developing neocortex.
source: Together with our imaging assays, these directed UV-CLIP experiments support the idea that both Pum2 and TDP-43 can directly interact with specific mRNAs encoding layer IV/V neuronal identity determinants in vivo in the cytoplasm of cells in the developing neocortex.
evidence: The claim is based on inference from the combined imaging and UV-CLIP data.

claim: Direct interaction of Pum2 and TDP-43 with Sox5, Bcl11b, and Rorb mRNAs could potentially mediate the post-transcriptional regulatory effects on translation.
source: This suggests that direct interaction of Pum2 and TDP-43 with these mRNAs could potentially mediate the post-transcriptional regulatory effects described above (Figure 9).
